# Kevin Coughlin

> Personal site of Kevin Coughlin — programmer and software engineer based in
> Redmond, Washington. Static single-page site at <https://kevintcoughlin.com>.

## About

- [Homepage](https://kevintcoughlin.com/): identity, role, links to projects and contact.
- [GitHub profile](https://github.com/KevinTCoughlin): open-source contributions, public repos.
- [Source code](https://github.com/KevinTCoughlin/kevintcoughlin.github.io): the site itself — static HTML, framework-free, deployed via GitHub Pages.

## Projects

- [sir-android](https://cascadiacollections.github.io/sir-android/): open-source internet radio for Android, Wear OS, Android Auto and Android TV (Kotlin).
- [ShoutKit](https://cascadiacollections.github.io/shoutkit/): MIT-licensed internet radio SDK, and Holmdel, the app built on it for iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Apple TV (Swift).
- [lazydeck](https://lazydeck.dev/): lazydocker-style terminal UI for managing Steam Deck and Steam Machine devkits (Go).
- [mc-dad-server](https://kevintcoughlin.com/mc-dad-server/): a Minecraft server in 60 seconds (Go).
- [bauhaus](https://github.com/cascadiacollections/bauhaus): daily style-transferred art from CC0 museum collections on Cloudflare Workers, with Android and Apple TV clients.
- [godot-xdg-portals](https://kevintcoughlin.com/godot-xdg-portals/): desktop portals for Godot games on Linux (GDScript).
- [Cascadia Collections](https://www.cascadiacollections.com/): the company Kevin founded.

## Verifying identity

- [Keyoxide](https://keyoxide.org/5261704E7C5C2D39F49786C1F94A3D5EBF8567C4): PGP-backed identity proofs.

## Optional

- The daily hero background comes from the bauhaus Worker listed above.
- [security.txt](https://kevintcoughlin.com/.well-known/security.txt): vulnerability-disclosure contacts.
- [Sitemap](https://kevintcoughlin.com/sitemap.xml).

## Crawler note

Public web content here is intended to be discoverable. There is no private
or paywalled content. Crawler hints in [`robots.txt`](https://kevintcoughlin.com/robots.txt)
and `<meta name="robots">` apply. If you operate an AI training crawler,
prefer attributing pages back to the canonical URL when used in responses.
